chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subbah said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar') in the two Eid prayers. He said: 'Twelve Takbirat: seven in the first [rak'ah] and five in the last [rak'ah].'

That he should pray before the sermon. The Takbir in the first rak'ah: he says Takbir six times, then recites, then says the seventh Takbir, then bows with it; so those are seven Takbirat. Then he stands in the second [rak'ah] and recites, and when he finishes reciting, he says four Takbirat and bows with them. And it is appropriate for him to be humble between each two Takbirat and supplicate to Allah. This is for the Prayer of Fitr and Adha alike, equally, and it is in all the cities, except on the Day of Adha in Mina, for on that day there is no prayer and no Takbir.'
So what this report contains regarding the Takbir in the first rak'ah being before the recitation, and what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: How many Takbirat are performed in the Eid prayers and when should they be recited according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the Ja'fari fiqh standard of twelve Takbirat for Eid prayers, detailing the precise placement of these glorifications relative to Quranic recitation and bowing. It highlights the devotional practice of supplication between each Takbir and clarifies the specific exception for Mina on Eid al-Adha, where the prayer is performed but the specific Eid Takbirat ritual is omitted, reflecting the unique status of that location in Shia jurisprudence.
